description:
## Destination

A written verdict on defk (`docs/verdict.md`). It covers a set of target workloads taken from the jobs people really write NIFs for, each in the catalog with an honest verdict against an optimised Elixir baseline. It also defines a kernel subset (language and runtime contract) good enough to express those workloads, with a developer experience where a kernel author can predict what is allowed and gets actionable errors when it isn't. The subset reference lives in `docs/language.md`. It is written so it could grow into a Hex library later; no packaging work happens now.

## Notes

- Domain: research into native kernels for Elixir. Glossary in `CONTEXT.md`; purpose and measurement rules in `AGENTS.md` and `examples/README.md`.
- Every session consults the skills "grilling" and "domain-modeling" (and "research" / "prototype" for those ticket types).
- Elixir first: defk only where it helps. Optimise and measure the Elixir side before claiming a defk win. Elixir wins are valid verdicts.
- Scope is demand-driven: a language feature, type or convenience construct is in only when a target workload needs it. Convenience constructs must be what an Elixir developer writes first, cost nothing over the hand loop, and keep Elixir's meaning.
- Devex bar for done: actionable compile errors (line, why, alternative); a subset reference listing every limit; the one rule: "A kernel is Elixir over numbers and binaries: it gives the result Elixir would, or raises where its types can't hold that result, or doesn't compile. It never gives a different answer." Limits allowed and documented; zero divergences.
- Never take down the BEAM: for any arguments a kernel returns or raises; it never starves or crashes the VM, and other processes keep running. No speed justifies breaking this (a port would be better). Done needs evidence for it next to the one rule.
- Pinned: no arbitrary-precision integers (i64 overflow stays `ArithmeticError`). Runtime contract is done apart from hardening and the question of state kept between calls.
- This map holds decisions. Build work stays in the existing beadwork roadmap (README "Roadmap"); the map points at it, it doesn't own it.
- Implementation plan: [Build to the defk verdict](defk-sgw) sequences the build tickets to docs/verdict.md; tickets are triaged ready-for-agent / ready-for-human / needs-triage.

## Decisions so far

- [Which jobs do people write NIFs for today?](defk-dtw.1): most NIFs wrap libraries (out of reach); defk's candidates are the long tail of hand-written loops over binaries, ranked: byte transforms, PCM mixing, sketch updates, f32 vectors, batched string distance, time-series encoding. Automatic yielding replaces the scheduling workarounds those NIFs hand-roll.
- [How do comparable native subsets keep their rules predictable?](defk-dtw.3): copy Numba's supported/restricted/unsupported reference with a separate divergence page, errors with a caret plus what, why and what to write instead, stable error codes linked to the reference, and tests that keep the reference true. Running in the host language helps debugging and testing but drifts unless semantics already match.
- [Where does Nx already cover native-speed numerics for Elixir?](defk-dtw.2): Nx owns whole-tensor numerics on large fixed-shape arrays; defk's niche is sequential/early-exit loops, variable-length byte work, and many concurrent mid-sized calls that must stay preemptible (no Nx backend yields).
- [What must docs/verdict.md contain to count as done?](defk-dtw.4): seven sections (conclusion with library go/no-go, a job guide, a frozen workload-results snapshot, runtime contract, devex with a cold test, limitations, method); every target workload gets a row on an optimised baseline, with the NIF/C, responsiveness and Nx (where relevant) beside the workload verdict; a go/no-go rule fixed in advance; done when the conclusion is accepted in a final session.
- [Choose the target workload set](defk-dtw.5): six workloads, each reproducing a real package's job against its own Elixir version and NIF: WebSocket masking, PCM mixing, HLL updates, cosine top-k over f32 (with Nx), batched Levenshtein, Gorilla encoding; tried roughly in that order of readiness (string distance first), nothing excluded up front; rolling_stats, geo_nearest and image_blur become supporting examples.
- [Should a kernel body also run as plain Elixir?](defk-dtw.6): yes, as Elixir mode: generated Elixir for tests and debugging, never a production fallback or baseline; it is normative (any disagreement is a bug or a listed divergence), so every kernel construct needs an Elixir meaning (array writes mean rebinding).
- [What does a good kernel compile error look like?](defk-dtw.8): Elixir's diagnostic frame with a caret, then why/hint lines (a rewrite that must compile) and a slug code linking docs/language.md; name the construct as written; report all rejections, capped at 10. Build handed off as [Adopt the kernel compile error format](defk-vku).
- [What is the one rule a kernel author keeps in their head?](defk-dtw.7): Elixir over numbers and binaries, Elixir's result or a raise or a compile error, never a different answer; limits allowed, divergences (aliasing, inf/NaN) must go; a value that doesn't fit its type raises, array writes included; no semantic opt-outs.
- [State kept between kernel calls: kernel-owned resources or binaries passed back in?](defk-dtw.9): binaries passed back in, a new binary or tuple out; never mutate an input; kernel-owned resources stay an expansion candidate; only HLL (registers) and Gorilla (scalar encoder state) carry state.
- [Should kernels offer opt-in wrapping integer arithmetic for hashes?](defk-dtw.10): no mode; masked arithmetic, band(expr, 2^k-1) written around the arithmetic and compiled wrapping with Elixir's exact result; a new u64/[u64] type for 64-bit hashes; Defk.Bits (clz, popcount, rotations) as plain Elixir functions.
- [Which open runtime issues are safety gaps?](defk-dtw.12): none of the four ticketed issues; a new one found, [alloc/2 size overflow crashes the VM](defk-gtv), is required for done; evidence is a [threat list with a test per entry](defk-5fc) plus a sanitizer run of the differential tests.
- [Is a C compiler at build time acceptable for a defk library?](defk-dtw.11): yes for app developers (as elixir_make packages); library authors would use cc_precompiler-style precompiled artefacts, named in the verdict but not built; no bundled compiler, Cranelift stays an exploration; evidence is [an actionable missing-compiler error](defk-lb8) and [a recorded mix release build](defk-ds0); cross-compiling is a listed limitation.
- [What do narrow element types ([f32], [i16], [i32]) mean in a kernel?](defk-dtw.13): [i16], [i32], [f32] as element types only, reads widen as Elixir does, f32 writes round as Elixir and raise only on inf, arithmetic always f64, native endianness, plain binaries for callers; inf/NaN input bits go to [Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels](defk-q1c); build is [Add [i16], [i32] and [f32] element types](defk-4ai).
- [Can a kernel produce variable-length bit output, and in what form?](defk-dtw.14): yes, the bitstring accumulator, acc = <<acc::bitstring, v::size(n)>> from <<>>, append-only, returned as a real bitstring; segment values that do not fit raise like array writes; Defk.Bits.f64_to_u64/1 for bit reinterpretation; build is [Add the bitstring accumulator](defk-cmr).
- [Plan the catalog build for the six target workloads](defk-dtw.15): anchors via pinned Mix.install; verdict at a pre-declared realistic size with sweep, NIF and tick-gap beside it; PCM becomes clip prevention, Levenshtein compares ex_strsim only; one ticket per workload under the catalog epic plus [Extend Defk.Bench.report/1 for target workloads](defk-9p6.10) and [Add u64, masked arithmetic and Defk.Bits](defk-wlu).
- [How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?](defk-dtw.16): Elixir mode applies the subset's limits so agreement is exact (=== values, bit-exact floats with -ffp-contract=off; raises by module and reason); StreamData edge-biased, workload and hostile-argument generators over catalog kernels, every subset test (Defk.Case) and docs/language.md examples; a Defk.Divergences registry that must be empty; deep and ASan/UBSan runs in a :peer node recorded in the verdict. Build: [Build Elixir mode](defk-v5d), then [Differential agreement checks](defk-63k).
- [Decide policy for inf/NaN inside kernels](defk-q1c): match Elixir with no limit or divergence; an accumulated, vectorisable isfinite flag on every float op and write (taken select arms only) raises ArithmeticError at exit or safepoint; non-finite input elements raise ArgumentError when read; build is [Raise on non-finite floats like Elixir](defk-i00).
- [Decide array value semantics (aliasing on write)](defk-i2e): value semantics through static copy-on-write (copy only where another binding is live; swaps copy nothing); input arrays writable by copy before the first write; an array write updates that variable through enclosing loops and branches, no other variable sees it; build is [Give arrays value semantics: copy on aliased write](defk-auo).
- [Does done need a per-kernel fast-path report?](defk-dtw.17): no; it is a catalog tool, not part of the devex bar or cold test: __defk_report__/0 data with defk's own fast-path decisions plus clang vectorisation remarks under report: :full; built on first need as [Add a fast-path report for kernels](defk-6cn).
- [Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?](defk-dtw.18): in: module attributes as constants, multi-clause kernels with a typed head, signed accumulator segments, the accumulator through helper kernels (Bitwise operator forms already in defk-w38); out with compile-error hints: |>, Enum aggregates, with_index/into:, <<>> field matches, the float-bits match, Enum.min over lists; builds are [Module attributes as constants in kernels](defk-ivt), [Multi-clause kernels with a typed function head](defk-u9c), [Signed integer segments in the bitstring accumulator](defk-dki), [Pass the bitstring accumulator through helper kernels](defk-ooq).

- [Should defk move to another implementation stack (Zig/Rust/V/Odin/Roc)?](defk-dtw.19): no. Node-crash isolation comes from prevention-by-construction and evidence (threat list, hostile-argument differential runs, sanitizers, hardening flags) plus the fault-containment spike (defk-7dm), not from the implementation language; all candidate languages funnel to the same LLVM optimizer, the frontend cannot move off Elixir AST, and a rewrite yields zero new verdict evidence at weeks of re-proof cost.

## Not yet specified

_(none)_

## Out of scope

- Expansion candidates (persistent structures via resources, parser scanning, CRC32C and pixel formats, per-pair and tiny calls, n-body, writing a wrapped library itself in defk): listed in the verdict under "Where defk could grow", not built in this map ([Choose the target workload set](defk-dtw.5)).
- Hex packaging, precompiled NIFs, and a semver promise (destination is a verdict that could grow into a library).
- Editor support: LSP diagnostics, formatter.
- UTF-8 strings as text, and maps (none of the six target workloads needs them; see Choose the target workload set).
- Calling back into Elixir from a kernel; concurrency inside a kernel.
- An upstream proposal to Elixir core or ERTS.

comments.text: Breadcrumb — external stack review (2026-10-08): a reviewer who had not seen defk recommended Zig/Rust/V/Odin/Roc. Evaluated against the four verdict dimensions and rejected (defk-dtw.19). Relevant facts for future changes: Zig/Rust/Odin compile via LLVM, V via C, so codegen quality cannot improve on current clang parity; erl_nif.h documents 'a native function that crashes will crash the whole VM' in every language; Rust safety stops at unsafe FFI; the Elixir frontend (macro, type checker, error format, Elixir mode) cannot move off Elixir AST at mix compile. The genuine alternative stack question is a codegen backend (defk-o1w, Cranelift), already scoped as exploration only per defk-dtw.11.

title: Wayfinder: roadmap to a defk verdict (kernel subset, runtime contract, devex)
